title: KAIST Prestige Scholarship for International Ph.D. Students (KPS)
official_source: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)
program_type: Graduate scholarship for international doctoral students, awarded automatically within the KAIST Scholarship scheme
duration: 8 regular semesters of support (from the start of the Ph.D. programme for Master's-Ph.D. Integrated entrants)
description: The KAIST Prestige Scholarship for International Ph.D. Students (KPS) is one of two named awards inside the KAIST Scholarship scheme for international graduate students, the other being the KAIST Global Presidential Scholarship (KGPS). KAIST's Office of Admissions states that KPS is open to international applicants in Master's-Ph.D. Integrated or Ph.D. programmes in all departments and provides full tuition coverage plus a monthly stipend of 300,000 KRW for eight regular semesters. title: UIC Admissions Scholarship (Underwood International College, Yonsei University)
program_type: Undergraduate admission merit scholarship (automatic consideration at application)
duration: Four years (8 semesters) of full tuition
description: The UIC Admissions Scholarship is awarded by Underwood International College of Yonsei University to newly admitted international undergraduates and covers the full tuition for four years. UIC publishes an International Students Track tuition of 8,202,000 KRW per semester for the 2026 academic year, which is the amount the scholarship waives. There is no separate scholarship application: candidates are considered automatically during admission and offers are sent individually with the admission packet. title: Yonsei International Companion Scholarship
program_type: Graduate School internal scholarship for international students (no separate application)
duration: Regular semesters: 4 semesters for master's and PhD programmes, 6 semesters for the integrated master's and PhD programme
description: The Yonsei International Companion Scholarship is a Graduate School award for full-time international students who entered through the international student admission track and are enrolled in regular semesters. title: KOICA Scholarship Program (Scholarship Program, CIAT)
official_source: Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) - Korean Government
program_type: Government-funded international postgraduate scholarship administered by KOICA under its CIAT fellowship programme
duration: Master's programmes are described by KOICA as seventeen months long; the Doctoral programme duration is not stated on the page fetched.

title: GIST Government-sponsored Scholarship
official_source: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology (GIST)
program_type: Automatic government/authority-funded graduate scholarship for all GIST students
duration: Master's scholarship benefit for a maximum of 4 enrolled semesters; the doctoral teaching-assistant benefit and the tuition support run to a maximum of 8 enrolled semesters.

title: TU Graz High Potentials Scholarship Programme
program_type: Partner-funded university scholarship programme for Bachelor's and Master's students
duration: Scholarships are awarded 'over a period of up to two years'
description: The TU Graz High Potentials scholarship programme supports young talent from Austria and abroad with scholarships of up to EUR 8,800 for Bachelor's students and up to EUR 17,600 for Master's students over a period of up to two years. The programme is funded by partner companies, so individual scholarships carry their own sponsor requirements in addition to TU Graz's general criteria. TU Graz publishes separate application windows for the two degree levels: 15 October 2026 to 15 February 2027 for the Master's scholarships and 5 May 2027 to 7 July 2027 for the Bachelor's scholarships. title: One World Scholarship (Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg)
program_type: Partial scholarship for international students from the Global South studying in Salzburg
duration: Paid monthly during the semester, October through June
description: The One World Scholarship of the Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg is a partial scholarship of EUR 500 per month during the semester (October through June) for students from Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East, Oceania, the Caribbean and Latin America who study in Salzburg. Applicants must already be enrolled in Austria or admitted to a regular degree programme, hold a student residence permit or visa, and be admitted to a regular Master's or PhD programme in Salzburg. Selection is a multi-stage process - online form until 12 July, verification of formal criteria, full application until 15 July
